# Differentiate the background of the In Review header

## Problem statement

In the Herdr work-item selection list, all group section headers (e.g. `── Group 1 (4) ▼ ──`, `── Idea (2) ──`, `── In Review (5) ──`) are rendered identically — bold, with a foreground stage colour and no background fill. The producer cannot distinguish the In Review section from other sections at a glance, which matters because In Review items are the only ones with an active producer-review obligation. Give the In Review header a grey background so the section stands out visually.

## Users

- **Herdr users (primarily the producer / session operator)** who scan the selection list for the In Review queue and need to locate that section quickly.
  - User story: "As a Herdr user reviewing the selection list, I want the In Review header to have a distinctive grey background so I can spot the review queue section immediately, even when the list is long."

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour, e.g. `ANSI.bg(238)` or a nearby grey value) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other group heading rows (e.g. `Group N`, `Idea`, `Completed`, etc.) are unchanged — no background fill added.
- AC3: The selected-heading highlight still works: when the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing reverse-video selection bar (`reverseWrap`) remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, count, collapse arrow, and width-truncation behaviour are unaffected by the background change (single-row heading invariant preserved).
- AC5: Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence, and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
- AC6: Full project test suite passes with the change.
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- Use existing ANSI helpers in `worklist.ts` (`ANSI.bg(code)` with a 256-colour code) — no new dependencies.
- Must not change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Implementation must be keyed off the heading's `groupLabel === 'In Review'` (the label originates in `grouping.ts`); keep the label source as the single source of truth.

## Existing state

- Group heading rows are first-class rows in the display-rows model (`DisplayHeadingRow`), interleaved by `WorkItemListState.getDisplayRows()` (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- The heading row is rendered in `createListRenderer` at `worklist.ts:~4482`:
  `const line = `${indent} ${ANSI.fg(stageColor(undefined))}${ANSI.bold}── ${row.groupLabel} (${row.count}) ${arrow} ──${ANSI.reset}``
- `ANSI.bg(code)` exists at `worklist.ts:~345` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`) and is already used for banner fills (e.g. `ANSI.bg(196)`, `ANSI.bg(220)`, `ANSI.bg(40)`).
- The `In Review` group label is assigned in `grouping.ts:~309` (`groupLabel: 'In Review'` for `stage === 'in_review'`).
- Selected rows are wrapped with `reverseWrap` (re-asserts `\x1b[0m` resets to keep the whole selected row highlighted); heading rows have no interior resets so they are handled fine.

## Desired change

- In the heading-row render branch of `createListRenderer`, when `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, wrap the line's base style with a grey background (`${ANSI.bg(238)}` or similar), keeping the existing foreground/bold styling and the existing `reverseWrap` interaction on selection. Other headings render as today.

## Key Files:

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch (`createListRenderer`, ~line 4482); add conditional grey background for `groupLabel === 'In Review'`; `ANSI.bg` helper at ~line 345.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — extend with tests asserting the background escape sequence on `In Review` headings and its absence on others.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `stageColor`/ANSI conventions (context only).

## Risks & assumptions

- Grey background may reduce contrast against the 220 (yellow-ish) foreground `stageColor` for in-review headings; mitigate by choosing a dark grey (238) and verifying readability. If contrast is insufficient, the foreground can be switched to white (231) for this heading only — record the choice in the implementation.
- Selection visibility: reverse-wrap must stay visible over the background — covered by AC3; verify selection rendering in a terminal, not just by string matching.
- Scope creep: do NOT extend the background to other headings unless separately requested — that is a separate work item (recorded here to avoid accidental bundling).
- Test brittleness: assert on the presence of the `\x1b[48;5;...m` background sequence for the In Review heading rather than on exact full-row strings, to avoid coupling to foreground/bold detail changes.

## Related work

- **Duplicate check performed** — no overlapping completed item found. Related completed items (none duplicates): WL-0MS4FIEN40037GB9 (total actionable count in Herdr header), WL-0MV6JGVPH009YDXB (in_progress/in_review in mandatory In Review set), WL-0MSBVS4AS006ZQEZ (selection-list refresh on tab focus), WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94 (heading rows as first-class display rows — this feature builds on that model).
- `docs/icons-design.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed description ("make the In Review header background gray (or similar) to differentiate that section from other sections") was specific enough to draft the brief directly. Assumption recorded: "gray (or similar)" means a grey ANSI 256 background (default candidate: 238, same value already used elsewhere in `worklist.ts`), applied only to the In Review heading; other section headers remain unchanged. Rationale: description explicitly scopes differentiation to "that section".

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MKW1GUSC1DSWYGS** – OpenCode (completed)
- **WL-0ML1LBF6H0NE40RX** – Fix TUI work item colors: use blessed markup instead of chalk ANSI codes (completed)
- **WL-0ML4DOK1U19NN8LG** – Add wl list --parent <id> for child-only listing (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CLI.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection, similar
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: background, extension, header, herdr, list, make, section, sections, selection

# Test: In Review heading background rendering

## Summary

Extend the heading-renderer unit tests to assert the grey background escape sequence on `In Review` headings, its absence on all other headings, and selection-bar-over-background behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: Unit tests cover the new rendering: a heading with label `In Review` contains the background escape sequence (the ANSI 256 prefix `\x1b[48;5;`, asserted on the escape prefix rather than the exact full-row string), and other headings do not; existing heading-render tests still pass.
- AC2: Headings with other labels (e.g. `Group 1`, `Idea`, `Completed`) render without any `\x1b[48;5;` background sequence.
- AC3: A selected `In Review` heading renders with the reverse-video selection bar (`\x1b[7m`) in addition to the grey background.
- AC4: All existing heading-render tests in `worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` continue to pass unchanged (single-row invariant, indentation, click-row mapping, line-count).
- AC5: Running the herdr test suite green with the new tests (via the project test skill).

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` — new tests added here; existing test content untouched.

## Implementation notes

- Add a `describe` block (e.g. "In Review heading background") following the file's existing style: `makeHeading` helper, `createListRenderer`, plain string-contains assertions.
- Assert on the `\x1b[48;5;` prefix for `In Review`; assert absence for `Group 1`/`Idea`/`Completed`.
- For the selection case, render with `selectedIndex` on the heading row and assert both `\x1b[7m` and `\x1b[48;5;` appear.
- These tests are expected to fail until the implementation feature (Grey background on In Review heading) lands — authored test-first (parent WL-0MUYJ8WJG0087VSU AC5).

## Deliverables

- Updated `worklist-renderer-headings.test.ts` covering AC1–AC3; existing tests unmodified (AC4); suite green (AC5).

## Dependencies

- None — must land before the implementation feature (test-first, parent WL-0MUYJ8WJG0087VSU).

# Grey background on In Review heading

## Summary

In `createListRenderer`'s heading-row branch, give the heading whose `groupLabel === 'In Review'` a grey ANSI 256 background fill while leaving every other heading unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The group heading row whose label is `In Review` renders with a grey background fill (ANSI 256-colour via the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper, default `ANSI.bg(238)`) in addition to its current bold/foreground styling.
- AC2: All other heading rows (`Group N`, `Idea`, `Other`, `Completed`, etc.) render exactly as before — no background escape added.
- AC3: When the In Review heading is the current selection, the existing `reverseWrap(line)` selection bar remains visible on top of the grey background.
- AC4: Heading text, item count, collapse arrow (`▼`/`▶`), depth indentation, and width truncation are unchanged; the single-row heading invariant and line-count accounting are preserved.
- AC5: The grey choice keeps the heading legible; if contrast against the existing foreground is insufficient, switch this heading's foreground to white (`ANSI.fg(231)`) and record the choice in a code comment.
- AC6: The full project test suite passes with the change (run via the project test skill).
- AC7: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (on the heading-render branch) and the relevant section of `packages/herdr/README.md` (and any relevant wiki or docs site entries).

## Constraints

- Use the existing `ANSI.bg(code)` helper in `worklist.ts` (`\x1b[48;5;${code}m`, ~line 357) — no new dependencies.
- Do NOT change the display-rows model, navigation, collapse logic, or line-count invariants (WL-0MSL5MPSZ003TG94).
- Key the condition off `row.groupLabel === 'In Review'`, keeping the label source (`grouping.ts` ~line 309) as the single source of truth.
- Do NOT extend the background to other headings — that is out of scope.

## Key Files

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — heading-row render branch in `createListRenderer` (~line 4482) and the `ANSI.bg` helper (~line 357).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — source of the `In Review` group label (~line 309); reference/consistency only.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Herdr UI conventions to update for AC7.

## Minimal implementation

- Add `const bg = row.groupLabel === 'In Review' ? ANSI.bg(238) : '';` in the heading branch and prepend it to the line's base style (keep foreground + bold + trailing `ANSI.reset`).

## Deliverables

- Updated `worklist.ts` heading render branch implementing AC1–AC5; doc/comment updates (AC7); suite green (AC6). Resolution of the grey/contrast choice recorded in a code comment (AC5).

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Test: In Review heading background rendering` (test-first ordering, parent AC5); dependency edge wired.
